<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-site-facts.py from the netra-mcp binary. Do not edit. -->

`netra-mcp` 0.30.1 registers **197 tools**: **137 read-only** and **60 mutating**. The mutating tools are not even listed unless `NETRA_MCP_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true` is set, and they keep the controller's own guards (plan token, risk confirmation, leases).

It also serves 6 prompts and 9 resources. See [MCP integration](../integrations/mcp-integration.md) for setup.

## Read-only tools

### ai

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_ai_agent` | Run the in-process natural-language graph: classify the question, optionally preview a deny/rate/allow draft, then synthesize a brief. |
| `netra_ai_ask` | Ask a natural-language question about the current Netra snapshot. |
| `netra_ai_brief` | Deterministic cluster network brief built from live agent/health/insights aggregates. |
| `netra_ai_digest` | On-call digest: severity, incident fingerprint, copy-paste card. |
| `netra_ai_draft` | Parse a natural-language deny/rate request into a preview eBPF rule. |
| `netra_ai_explain` | Narrate one structured finding (kind/subject/message/page) against the live snapshot. |
| `netra_ai_status` | Whether the optional LLM rewrite path is configured. |
| `netra_ai_suggestions` | Live follow-up questions derived from the current snapshot (stale agents, DNS, exposure, lease). |

### audit

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_audit_summary` | Rollup of the audit log by actor, action, and hour. |

### capture

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_capture_status` | Every node with an active packet-capture session: filter, snap length, requestor, start/expiry time. |
| `netra_capture_summaries` | Bounded metadata for active and recent capture sessions (frame counts, protocol buckets, duration). |

### core

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_agents` | List all reporting Netra agents (one per node) with their latest status and staleness. |
| `netra_audit` | List recent Netra audit events: every mutating action taken through the controller API, including by this MCP server, with actor/action/target. |
| `netra_baselines` | Whether behavior and rate baselines exist and how old they are. |
| `netra_compliance` | CIS-inspired network hardening pack from sysctl-audit. |
| `netra_fleet` | Compact per-node agent inventory. |
| `netra_handoff` | On-call pack: report + playbook + coverage + fleet + audit + drop reasons. |
| `netra_incidents` | Cross-signal incident clusters: health anomalies, behavior/rate drift, exposure, drop-detective findings, and audit events joined by a shared canonical source (workload/pod/cgroup/node), only surfaced once at least two different signal kinds agree on the same source. |
| `netra_lease` | Enforce-mode lease clock: remaining seconds, expired, or none. |
| `netra_netlink` | Read-only RTNL change recorder: link, address, route, neighbor events and optional per-node state snapshots. |
| `netra_playbooks` | Review-only operator playbook derived from the current report snapshot. |
| `netra_pods` | List pods known to the cluster, with lockdown status. |
| `netra_ports` | Top destination ports by packet count (protocol/port). |
| `netra_protocols` | L4 protocol mix (TCP/UDP/…) across current destination stats. |
| `netra_report` | Point-in-time operator briefing (health, drift, exposure, incidents, recent audit). |
| `netra_scorecard` | Single 0-100 board from health, stale agents, detached programs, missing maps, blocked events. |
| `netra_status` | Overall Netra controller status: fast-path config, agent counts/staleness, baseline and rate-baseline capture state, Hubble status, HA/Cilium flags. |
| `netra_talkers` | Top destination IPs by packet count across current agent reports. |
| `netra_vms` | List KubeVirt VMs known to the cluster, with lockdown status. |

### ebpf

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_ebpf_ai_destinations` | Observe known GenAI/MCP SaaS destinations via SNI/HTTP Host/DNS metadata. |
| `netra_ebpf_app_categories` | Heuristic CDN/SaaS/cloud category labels from SNI/Host/DNS metadata. |
| `netra_ebpf_attachments` | Read-only BPF attachment inventory and hook drift per node. |
| `netra_ebpf_auto_mitigate` | Status of optional volumetric auto-mitigation (conn-rate / Shield / leased deny). |
| `netra_ebpf_auto_mitigate_preview` | Shadow preview of volumetric auto-mitigate candidates from current scan findings and UDP deltas. |
| `netra_ebpf_capabilities` | Static manifest of this Netra deployment's eBPF hooks, observability signals, and enforcement capabilities, including per-rule-type map capacity limits. |
| `netra_ebpf_capdrift` | Capability-change anomalies (effective-capability gain/loss) on processes the eBPF datapath already tracks — agent-sourced from a periodic /proc scan (requires NETRA_PROCMETA_ENABLED on the agent), not a live kernel credential read. |
| `netra_ebpf_census` | Counts of deny/allow list entries. |
| `netra_ebpf_config` | The live eBPF fast-path configuration (mode, all blocked IPs/CIDRs/ports/UIDs/DNS/processes/SNI, rate limits, workload scopes). |
| `netra_ebpf_coverage` | Per-node hook/program coverage matrix: attached vs detached programs, missing maps, stale agents. |
| `netra_ebpf_deny_preview` | Review-only blast radius for a proposed emergency deny. |
| `netra_ebpf_deny_preview_history` | Review-only historical blast radius for a proposed emergency deny against the controller flowlog (up to 7 days). |
| `netra_ebpf_diagnose` | Drop-detective findings: likely root causes for observed drops, correlated with the current fast-path config. |
| `netra_ebpf_dns_findings` | Metadata-only DNS anomaly findings (tunneling, DGA, beaconing, NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL storms) from a continuously-running detector fed by matched DNS-response events. |
| `netra_ebpf_drops` | Drop diagnostics aggregated from kernel skb drop-reason counters across agents. |
| `netra_ebpf_encrypted_dns` | DoT (port 853) and known DoH SaaS destinations from metadata. |
| `netra_ebpf_exehash` | Executable-content-hash-change anomalies on processes the eBPF datapath already tracks — a live process's on-disk binary content changing while it runs. |
| `netra_ebpf_health` | Network health diagnostics and anomalies derived from agent reports (TCP health, retransmits, connect latency, etc.). |
| `netra_ebpf_interfaces` | Per-interface flow attribution: packets/bytes/blocked and top destinations per network interface, from Netra's TC/TCX-attached hooks only (not cgroup or XDP-early-deny traffic). |
| `netra_ebpf_ipv6` | IPv6 extension-header and fragmentation diagnostics: extension-header counts, fragmentation rate, and truncated-chain counts per node, with anomaly detection. |
| `netra_ebpf_l7` | Best-effort L7 observability: TLS SNI, cleartext HTTP/1 method+Host, and HTTP/1 status when the status line starts the packet. |
| `netra_ebpf_maps` | Read-only inventory of datapath map contents (controller desired state under /sys/fs/bpf/netra): deny/allow/rate/policy entries with human labels, counts, and limits. |
| `netra_ebpf_nsdrift` | Network-namespace-change anomalies on processes the eBPF datapath already tracks — a live process moving network namespaces after start (setns), agent-sourced from the same periodic /proc scan capability-drift uses (requires NETRA_PROCMETA_ENABLED). |
| `netra_ebpf_path` | Path diagnostics: per-hop/per-hook health signals for traffic across the cluster. |
| `netra_ebpf_reasons` | Histogram of FastPathEvent action/reason pairs. |
| `netra_ebpf_rules_get` | Get one eBPF fast-path rule by its stable ID. |
| `netra_ebpf_rules_history` | Revision history for one eBPF fast-path rule's edits (via netra_ebpf_rules_patch), each with a before/after snapshot. |
| `netra_ebpf_rules_list` | List every eBPF fast-path deny rule (exact IP, CIDR, port, UID, process, DNS, SNI, rate limit) with its stable ID, so it can be referenced by netra_ebpf_rules_patch/_delete/_history instead of the legacy value-keyed add/delete tools. |
| `netra_ebpf_scan_findings` | Port-scan, fan-out, lateral-movement, and SYN-flood findings from a continuously-running detector fed by per-connection-attempt TCP flag data. |
| `netra_ebpf_scope_preview` | Preview which pods would match a set of eBPF workload scopes, without changing the active scope (see netra_ebpf_scope_set to apply). |
| `netra_ebpf_shield` | XDP Shield diagnostics: allowed/dropped/audited traffic broken out by class (SYN/UDP/ICMP/other) per node, plus the top offending sources across the cluster, with anomaly detection. |
| `netra_ebpf_stack_histograms` | Observe-only softirq/softnet pressure and listen-queue depth buckets from agent reports. |
| `netra_ebpf_summary` | A high-level rollup of eBPF fast-path activity across all agents. |
| `netra_ebpf_sysctl_audit` | Network-hardening/tuning sysctl inventory across agents: per-interface security posture (rp_filter, redirects, source-route, martians, proxy_arp), IPv6 posture, TCP tuning/lifecycle, conntrack timeouts, and ARP/neighbor/bridge settings, flagged against an established hardening baseline where one exists. |
| `netra_ebpf_tls_fingerprint_risk` | Rare JA3 / missing-SNI / ECH-extension risk board from capture fingerprints. |
| `netra_ebpf_tls_fingerprints` | JA3/JA4 fingerprints observed from capture-stream ClientHello frames (single-skb). |
| `netra_ebpf_topology` | A derived service/workload topology view built from current agent reports. |
| `netra_ebpf_workloads` | List workload identities (pod/cgroup/container attribution) known to the cluster, optionally for one node. |

### export

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_export_audit` | Export recent audit events for a SIEM or log pipeline. |
| `netra_export_blocks` | Export current blocked/dropped FastPathEvents (5-tuple + reason + process identity) in the SIEM encodings, including otlp-trace — each blocked event becomes one OTLP span for a trace-based backend. |
| `netra_export_events` | Export current health anomalies and incident clusters (optionally audit) in the same SIEM encodings as netra_export_audit. |
| `netra_export_flows` | Export current non-stale destination-flow counters (5-tuple + packets/bytes/blocked) in the SIEM encodings. |
| `netra_export_status` | Whether optional syslog push is configured, plus the pull-export endpoints and encodings this controller supports. |

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_insights_baseline_get` | The currently captured behavior baseline, if any (see netra_insights_baseline_capture to create one). |
| `netra_insights_blast_radius` | Multi-hop reachability from one dependency-graph node, breadth-first over observed traffic edges. |
| `netra_insights_category_deny` | Review-only leased SNI deny drafts for selected app categories (default social,finance). |
| `netra_insights_dependencies` | The inferred service dependency graph (who talks to whom, including external destinations). |
| `netra_insights_destination_risk` | Combined destination risk from intel hits, categories, AI/MCP, DoH/DoT, and volume. |
| `netra_insights_drift` | Behavior drift findings: how current traffic differs from the captured baseline. |
| `netra_insights_ech_blind` | ECH / missing-SNI blindness board. |
| `netra_insights_exfil` | Exfil heuristics: destination fan-out, volume, rare hosts. |
| `netra_insights_experience` | Workload digital-experience scorecard from connect latency, TCP retrans/RTO, DNS failures. |
| `netra_insights_exposure` | Exposure findings combining the dependency graph with behavior and rate drift (e.g. |
| `netra_insights_health_trend` | Linear time-to-breach projection from recent cluster health-score history. |
| `netra_insights_identity_drafts` | ServiceAccount + label identity drafts with review-only CNP sketches. |
| `netra_insights_kernel_notes` | Scrubbed kernel log lines about netdev, TCP, UDP, conntrack, and OOM. |
| `netra_insights_lateral` | Lateral-movement playbooks from scan findings with review-only lease drafts. |
| `netra_insights_microseg` | East-west microsegmentation guidance: prefer PacketWolf on Cilium; Netra lease drafts only when Cilium is absent. |
| `netra_insights_new_since_start` | Behavior-drift findings (new destinations since the captured baseline) whose owning pod/workload started after that baseline — a plausible "first egress after start" correlation, not a precise timing claim (no conversion exists between kernel-boot-monotonic packet timestamps and Kubernetes wall-clock pod start times). |
| `netra_insights_policy_packs` | Review-only sanctioned-egress CiliumNetworkPolicy packs from NETRA_SANCTIONED_HOSTS + observed traffic. |
| `netra_insights_policy_review` | Full review for one policy recommendation (from netra_insights_recommendations): which live CiliumNetworkPolicy actually governs the workload (best-effort label match, may be ambiguous), a semantic diff against it, a traffic-aware blast-radius check for each destination the diff would remove (CIDR destinations checked against live traffic; FQDN/entity destinations honestly marked "could not correlate", never a false negative), and recent policy revision history. |
| `netra_insights_profiles` | Bounded kernel stacks for the hottest host comms, plus the kernel wait channel (wchan). |
| `netra_insights_protocol_downgrades` | Workload/host pairs with TLS handshake history at baseline capture time that now also show cleartext HTTP to the same host. |
| `netra_insights_rate_baseline_get` | The currently captured traffic-rate baseline, if any (see netra_insights_rate_baseline_capture to create one). |
| `netra_insights_rate_drift` | How current traffic rates differ from the captured rate baseline. |
| `netra_insights_rates` | Current traffic-rate window (packets/bytes per second) across agents. |
| `netra_insights_recommendations` | Suggested NetworkPolicy changes derived from the dependency graph and observed behavior. |
| `netra_insights_red` | Per-workload rate, errors, and TCP SRTT over a window. |
| `netra_insights_remediations` | Proposed remediations combining exposure and drift findings. |
| `netra_insights_shadow_saas` | Shadow SaaS / unsanctioned destinations from SNI/Host/DNS vs NETRA_SANCTIONED_HOSTS. |
| `netra_insights_summary` | Rollup counts across dependency graph, behavior drift, rate drift, exposure, and remediation insights. |
| `netra_insights_traces` | Inferred service-path spans from flow edges and pod IPs. |
| `netra_insights_workload_events` | Kubernetes Warning events for pods (OOMKilled, probe failures, BackOff). |
| `netra_insights_zero_trust` | Identity-aware Zero Trust allow/deny drafts from live workload traffic. |

| Tool | What it does |

## Mutating tools (opt in)

Listed only when `NETRA_MCP_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true`. Each call is attributed to `NETRA_MCP_ACTOR`.

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `netra_capture_start` | Start a packet-capture session on one node. |
| `netra_capture_stop` | Stop an active packet-capture session on one node before its duration expires. |
| `netra_ebpf_ai_destinations_deny` | Lease-deny currently observed GenAI/MCP SaaS SNI hosts. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_add` | Add an exact IPv4 or IPv6 exception. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_cidr_add` | Add a CIDR exception evaluated before deny/rate. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_cidr_delete` | Remove a CIDR exception. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_delete` | Remove an allow-list exception. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_port_add` | Add an L4 port exception evaluated before deny/CIDR/port/rate. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_port_delete` | Remove an L4 port exception. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_process_add` | Add a process name (Linux "comm", up to 15 bytes) exception evaluated before UID/comm deny at the socket hook. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_process_delete` | Remove a process name exception. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_uid_add` | Add a Linux UID exception evaluated before UID/comm deny at the socket hook. |
| `netra_ebpf_allow_uid_delete` | Remove a UID exception. |
| `netra_ebpf_capability_add` | Deny new socket() attempts for any process with a given Linux capability currently effective (CAP_NET_RAW/CAP_NET_ADMIN only — a small, fixed vocabulary, not arbitrary capability names). |
| `netra_ebpf_capability_delete` | Remove a capability-gated socket deny entry. |
| `netra_ebpf_cidr_add` | Add a CIDR to the eBPF fast-path CIDR deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_cidr_delete` | Remove a CIDR from the eBPF fast-path CIDR deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_conn_rate_limit_add` | Cap new TCP connection attempts per second for every workload matching a selector (namespace/pod/owner/labels — same shape as netra_ebpf_scope_set). |
| `netra_ebpf_conn_rate_limit_delete` | Delete a connection-rate-limit rule by its id (from the fast-path config's connRateLimits, or netra_ebpf_conn_rate_limit_add's response). |
| `netra_ebpf_deny_add` | Add an exact IPv4 or IPv6 address to the eBPF deny list (blocks all traffic to/from it). |
| `netra_ebpf_deny_delete` | Remove an address from the eBPF deny list. |
| `netra_ebpf_dns_add` | Add an exact plain-DNS query name (over UDP/53) to the eBPF deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_dns_delete` | Remove a DNS name from the eBPF deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_mode` | Switch the eBPF fast path between "observe" (monitor only) and "enforce" (actively block). |
| `netra_ebpf_netpol_config_set` | Enable or disable the legacy per-workload NetPol-emulation deny engine (independent of the eBPF fast-path deny-list, and independent of the v2 allow/default-deny engine below). |
| `netra_ebpf_netpol_default_deny_plan` | Mandatory first step to activate/deactivate v2 default-deny for a workload selector: assesses risk (workloads with zero covering allow rules make this "critical" and the call is refused unless allow_no_rules is set) and issues a receipt.token (5-minute, single-use) required by netra_ebpf_netpol_default_deny_set. |
| `netra_ebpf_netpol_default_deny_set` | Activate or deactivate v2 default-deny for a workload selector. |
| `netra_ebpf_netpol_rule_add` | Add a v2 allow/deny rule for workloads matching a selector (namespace/pod/owner/labels — same shape as netra_ebpf_scope_set), exact IPv4 peer only. |
| `netra_ebpf_netpol_rule_delete` | Delete a v2 allow/deny rule by its id (from the fast-path config's netPolRules, or netra_ebpf_netpol_rule_add's response). |
| `netra_ebpf_netpol_v2_config_set` | Enable or disable the v2 per-workload allow-list/default-deny engine (independent of the legacy NetPol-emulation deny engine above). |
| `netra_ebpf_port_add` | Add a port to the eBPF fast-path port deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_port_delete` | Remove a port from the eBPF fast-path port deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_process_add` | Add a process name (Linux "comm", up to 15 bytes) to the eBPF deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_process_delete` | Remove a process name from the eBPF deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_rate_delete` | Remove the rate limit for an IPv4 or IPv6 destination. |
| `netra_ebpf_rate_set` | Set a packets-per-second and/or bytes-per-second rate limit for an exact IPv4 or IPv6 destination — at least one of pps/bps is required (the server refuses an all-zero rule as a no-op). |
| `netra_ebpf_rules_delete` | Delete one eBPF fast-path rule by its stable ID — a thin wrapper resolving to the same store mutation the legacy value-keyed delete tools use. |
| `netra_ebpf_rules_patch` | Edit one eBPF fast-path rule in place by its stable ID (from netra_ebpf_rules_list), preserving the ID and recording a before/after revision (see netra_ebpf_rules_history). |
| `netra_ebpf_rules_rollback` | Undo one specific edit to a rule: restores the value it had before that revision (from netra_ebpf_rules_history), recorded as a new revision rather than rewriting history. |
| `netra_ebpf_scope_set` | Set which workloads the eBPF fast path applies to: "all" (cluster-wide) or "selected" (only the given scopes). |
| `netra_ebpf_shield_set` | Configure the XDP DDoS shield: a per-source-class (SYN/UDP/ICMP/other) PPS token-bucket rate limiter, independent of the eBPF fast-path deny-list and its own mode. |
| `netra_ebpf_sni_add` | Add an exact TLS SNI name to the eBPF deny rule set (best-effort, requires ClientHello SNI parsing). |
| `netra_ebpf_sni_delete` | Remove a TLS SNI name from the eBPF deny rule set. |
| `netra_ebpf_syn_drop_add` | Flag an exact-IP deny entry (blockedIPv4/blockedIPv6 for egress, blockedIngressIPv4/blockedIngressIPv6 for ingress) for SYN-drop mode: only a genuinely new TCP connection attempt is dropped for that address+direction; any other TCP packet is allowed through instead of unconditionally dropped. |
| `netra_ebpf_syn_drop_delete` | Remove a SYN-drop-mode flag, reverting that exact-IP deny entry to dropping every packet (not just new SYNs). |
| `netra_ebpf_uid_add` | Add a Linux UID to the eBPF fast-path deny rule set (blocks all sockets opened by that UID). |
| `netra_ebpf_uid_delete` | Remove a UID from the eBPF fast-path deny rule set. |
| `netra_insights_baseline_capture` | Capture a new behavior baseline from current agent reports, replacing any existing one. |
| `netra_insights_baseline_clear` | Clear the captured behavior baseline. |
| `netra_insights_rate_baseline_capture` | Capture a new traffic-rate baseline over a window of current agent reports, replacing any existing one. |
| `netra_insights_rate_baseline_clear` | Clear the captured traffic-rate baseline. |
| `netra_intel_apply` | Import the active threat-intel feed into deny maps. |
| `netra_intel_feed_put` | Replace the active threat-intel feed (JSON/CSV/bare list). |
| `netra_policy_apply` | Apply a CiliumNetworkPolicy manifest. |
| `netra_policy_delete` | Delete a CiliumNetworkPolicy from the cluster. |
| `netra_policy_gitops_resync` | Explicitly apply a candidate manifest via the GitOps pipeline, bypassing the reconciler's own auto-apply gating (drift or high/critical risk) — the human override for a manifest netra_policy_gitops_status shows as pending. |
| `netra_policy_history_import` | Import a previously exported policy revision archive (from netra_policies_history_export). |
| `netra_policy_plan` | Dry-run a CiliumNetworkPolicy manifest change against the live cluster and risk-assess it. |
| `netra_policy_rollback` | Roll a CiliumNetworkPolicy back to a previously recorded revision (from netra_policies_history). |
| `netra_policy_unlock` | Remove an applied lockdown (deny-all) policy for a workload, restoring its normal network access. |
